chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarakhsi narrated to us, saying: Abu Lubaid Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isra'il narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Al-Ifriqi narrated from Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) said:

There will come upon my nation that which came upon the Children of Israel, equal by equal. Indeed, they were divided into seventy-two sects, and my nation will be divided into seventy-three sects; they will add one above those. All of them are in the Fire, except for one. He said: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is that one? He said: It is what we are upon today, me and my companions.
ai.seo_question: What are the 73 sects in Shia hadith and which one is saved?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* establishes the foundational Shia doctrine of the 'Saving Sect' (al-Firqa al-Najiya) by linking the Ummah's fragmentation to the historical precedent of Bani Israel. While the Prophet identifies the saved group as those adhering to his own understanding and that of his companions, Shia scholars traditionally interpret this as the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing their continuity with the Prophet's true teachings. The mention of 'seventy-three' sects highlights the inevitability of doctrinal diversity, with the 'one' representing the authentic path of Imamate and Sunnah.
